subject: microbiology
intro: Microbiology follows the smallest living things into medicine, food, water and industry — wherever bacteria, viruses and fungi cause problems, and wherever they solve them.

roles.title: Microbiologists
roles.what: Investigate the growth, structure and development of microscopic organisms such as bacteria, algae and fungi — including medical microbiologists who study how organisms relate to disease and how antibiotics act on them.
roles.where: The course is the job description: prokaryotic cell structure, microbial metabolism and growth curves, the Gram-positive and Gram-negative systematics of unit 6, and the antimicrobials-and-resistance unit.

roles.title: Epidemiologists
roles.what: Investigate the determinants and distribution of disease, disability and health outcomes in populations, and develop the means for their prevention and control.
roles.where: Unit 7 — portals of entry, virulence factors and epidemiological methods — teaches the disease-distribution logic of outbreak investigation, with the nosocomial and emerging-infections topic as the daily caseload.

roles.title: Biological Technicians
roles.what: Assist scientists by setting up and maintaining laboratory equipment, monitoring experiments, collecting data and samples, making observations and calculating and recording results, sometimes analysing organic substances.
roles.where: Microscopy and staining from unit 1, culture and growth-curve measurement from unit 3, and genetic engineering with microbes from unit 4 are the hands-on laboratory skills that support working scientists.

roles.title: Biological Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the biological sciences — lecturing, running laboratory sessions and designing assessments — often while leading research on the organisms and systems they teach.
roles.where: Teaching microbial genetics, diversity, pathogenesis and applied microbiology is literally this course's arc, and the textbook chapter structure gives you a ready map of the introductory courses you would lead.
